title: Rabbi Tachlifa (a Palestinian Amora)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7:2: “Rabbi Nasa said: At times I ate with Rabbi Tachlifa, Father, and with Aninaya bar Sisi, my uncle.” Hyman calls the word “Father” a scribal error, for at the end of Terumot Rabbi Nasa said: “I did not know Father; Mother used to tell me, ‘Your father used to say,’” etc.

The Berakhot statement is cited in Bereshit Rabbah 91:3, and there: “Rabbi Asa (Hyman proposes Nasa) said: Many times I ate with Rabbi Tachlifa, and many times I ate with Rabbi Chanina (Hyman proposes Aninaya) bar Sisi, my uncle.” Hyman suggests that perhaps he is Rav Tachlifa, the student of Rav Huna and Rav Chisda, who went up to the Land of Israel.

notes.text: חביבי is rendered my uncle, not my dear one. Saved Guggenheimer English Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7:2 has father Tachlifa and uncle Aninia; saved Sefaria English Bereshit Rabbah 91:3 has Tachlifa and uncle Chanina. Hyman’s rejection of Father, Asa/Nasa and Chanina/Aninaya corrections, and possible Babylonian identification remain his proposals; neither named digital witness is silently harmonized.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 7:2 preserves Nassa, Tachlifa as father, and Aninaya as uncle. Hyman’s rejection of “Father,” Asa/Nasa and Chanina/Aninaya corrections, and possible identification with the Babylonian Tachlifa remain his proposals.
